question: Should ClawHub sign the existing stored hosted feed contract, and what key/trust-root and schema version should OpenClaw clients trust?
rationale: Feed signing changes a client trust boundary and production key-management contract; the current specs explicitly leave signing as a separate production decision, so routine code review cannot choose the permanent security model.

options.title: Sign Stored Publications
options.body: Require signing to wrap the current stored `catalogFeedPublications` payload, preserve exact version/integrity semantics, and document the public key/trust-root rollout before merge.

options.title: Approve A Versioned Signed Feed
options.body: Maintainers can approve a new schema/versioned endpoint after confirming matching OpenClaw parser support and documenting compatibility behavior.

options.title: Pause Signing
options.body: Keep this draft paused until the feed signing RFC, production secrets, and client trust root are ready to land together.

recommendation.title: Sign Stored Publications
recommendation.body: Require signing to wrap the current stored `catalogFeedPublications` payload, preserve exact version/integrity semantics, and document the public key/trust-root rollout before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged hosted-feed work introduced the current feed contract and explicitly split signing into a separate production decision.
